messages.content:
How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide that shows **two** ways to hit the “Get information of device connector versions” API on a Cisco Nexus Dashboard instance that is running **v6.3.1**: | Method | What you’ll need | How to do it | |--------|------------------|--------------| | **A. Use the built‑in API Explorer** | • A browser session logged into the Dashboard
• The API Explorer UI (available in v6.3.1) | 1. Log in to the Dashboard.
2. Click the **“API Explorer”** icon (or go to `/api-explorer`).
3. In the top‑right corner choose **“v6.3.1”** from the drop‑down list.
4. Expand the **“Device Connector”** section and locate the **“GET /deviceConnectorVersions”** endpoint.
5. Click **“Try it out”** – the UI will auto‑populate required headers (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer `).
6. If there are optional query parameters (e.g., `page`, `size`), enter values or leave blank.
7. Hit **“Execute”**. The response pane will show the JSON payload and status code. | | **B. Call it programmatically (curl / Postman)** | • Base URL of your Dashboard (e.g., `https://nexus.example.com`)
• An access token (OAuth2 bearer token)
• Optional query params | 1. Get a bearer token (see below).
2. Build the full URL:
```bash\n https:///api/v1/deviceConnectorVersions\n ```
3. Add query params if needed, e.g.:
```bash\n https:///api/v1/deviceConnectorVersions?page=0&size=20\n ```
4. Execute with curl:
```bash\n curl -X GET \\\n -H \"Accept: application/json\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n \"https:///api/v1/deviceConnectorVersions\"\n ```
5. Inspect the JSON output and HTTP status. | --- ### Getting an Access Token (OAuth2) The Nexus Dashboard uses OAuth2 bearer tokens for API calls. Here’s a minimal flow: ```bash # 1. Obtain a client ID & secret from the Dashboard admin console # 2. Request a token (replace placeholders) curl -X POST \ -d "grant_type=password&username=&password=" \ -u ":" \ https:///oauth/token ``` The response will contain an `access_token`. Copy that value and paste it into the `Authorization` header shown above. --- ### Using the Provided Tool (`requests_get`) If you already know the exact endpoint URL, you can let me call it for you. Just give me the full URL (including any query parameters) and I’ll invoke the `requests_get` function. For example: ```json { "url": "https://nexus.example.com/api/v1/deviceConnectorVersions", "params": { "page": 0, "size": 20 } } ``` I’ll then return the raw JSON response so you can inspect it directly. --- #### Quick Recap 1. **Login → API Explorer → v6.3.1 → GET /deviceConnectorVersions → Try it out → Execute** 2. OR **curl/Postman** with `Authorization: Bearer ` and the endpoint `/api/v1/deviceConnectorVersions`. That’s all you need to pull the device connector version information from a Cisco Nexus Dashboard running v6.3.1!
